relevance_note: A case report of Rosenthal fibre encephalopathy (out of scope) with a literature table of 15 published adult cases the authors classify as Alexander's disease ("Of these, 15 patients had Alexander's disease"), plus a few individually described Alexander disease cases in the Discussion and Note added in proof.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script (scratch dir) assembled the JSON, cutting each table span from the start of the Markdown row through the quoted cell so spans stay verbatim; I checked every row and value against Table 1 by eye. The first-hand case (32-year-old man with AIDS) is Rosenthal fibre encephalopathy, not Alexander disease, and gets no row; nor do the 10 published RFE cases in Table 1, including the 22-year-old man (ref 12) and the '§78 Female 17' case the authors reclassify as possible RFE although its original authors had tentatively called it senile-onset Alexander's disease. In scope: the 15 published cases in the 'Diagnosis of Alexander's disease' section of Table 1; two cases from refs 18 20 (alive at 48 and 20 years); the ref 21 adult-onset case (onset 45 years); and the two Japanese brothers in the Note added in proof. Labels: Table 1 has no label column, so 'Table 1 row k', counting patient rows only within the table (the section-heading rows 'Diagnosis of ...' are not counted), so the Alexander's disease cases are rows 1-15. The 'Age and sex' cell holds age, sex and the superscript reference number (footnote: 'The numeric reference to each case is indicated in superscript'); the reference goes in source_reference_in_review. The table does not say what the age is (onset, death or report; the text calls 23-61 years 'the age range of adult onset Alexander's disease'), so it is recorded as age at last evaluation/time of report, and onset is left not reported. CONVERSION DEFECT: the Markdown row '| 43 Female 25 48 Female 16 |' merges two printed rows (43 Female ref 25 and 48 Female ref 16), and the next row '49 Female 16' carries spill-over text ('quadriparesis, ataxia, urinary and faecal incontinence Bulbar palsy, palatal myoclonus'); I split the merged row into rows 13 and 14 by the two age/sex strings but did not assign any systemic, neurological or postmortem cell to rows 13, 14 or 15, because the cell alignment is broken (same caution as D-31 for stacked values); all their features are not reported. Row 6 (23 Female ref 4) has '+' under 'Neurological involvement - No', recorded as 'neurological involvement' excluded with the column header as second span; no specific checklist item is excluded from it. Pathology findings from the 'Postmortem CNS findings' column are recorded as observed features with detail 'postmortem CNS finding'; rows 7 and 8 carry '*', which the legend defines as findings on brain biopsy. 'Demyelination' and 'cavitating brain lesions' have no stated location (cerebral vs other), so the checklist item 'cerebral white matter abnormality' is left not reported; 'calcified basal ganglia' sets 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality' observed. Mappings to checklist: epilepsy/childhood seizures -> seizures; dementia -> cognitive decline; nystagmus -> eye movement abnormality; palatal myoclonus -> palatal tremor; urinary incontinence -> autonomic dysfunction; spastic monoparesis -> limb weakness and spasticity; dysphonia -> dysarthria or dysphonia. Bulbar palsy was not mapped to dysphagia or dysarthria. Vital status is left not reported for Table 1 cases although postmortem findings imply death, because the paper does not state it per person. Only the two Namekawa brothers have a GFAP variant tied to them, and no variant is printed ('novel missense mutations', plural, for two brothers; whether they share one variant is not stated), so each gets a variant row with variant_original_string 'not reported' and type 'missense' from the named-group statement; which brother had postmortem confirmation is not stated. The text says GFAP mutations 'have yet to be shown in any cases of adult onset, including the cases cited in table 1', so Table 1 cases get no variant rows; the ref 21 case had known mutations excluded by limited analysis (no variant row); the refs 18 20 cases are not stated to carry a mutation (no variant row) and their disease label is left not reported because the sentence names only 'the latter molecular genetic studies'. The paper says four familial cases from refs 15 and 16 lacked pathological confirmation 'as the diagnosis had been confirmed in the other siblings', but names no individuals, so no family labels or sibling links were recorded. n_patients_reported = 2 (the brothers, the only people described with GFAP variants); cohort_size_as_stated = 25 (published patients found by the Medline search, excluding the present case). Contradictions: none found within the paper; the text gives the AxD count as 15, matching 15 printed age/sex strings in that section.
